messages:
alice.kim: heads-up — saw an ECC spike on eu-west1-gpu-12 at 02:11 UTC. nodebot auto-annotated and cordoned, but a couple k8s gpu-pods (kv-cache heavy) were abruptly evicted and slurm jobs didn't transfer cleanly.
nodebot: automated signal: GPU_ECC_BURST on eu-west1-gpu-12 -> applied soft-cordon; emitted event id=ecc-2331234567. see /alerts/eu-west1
devops-oncall: pinging @ben.turner and @carla.nguyen for slurm<>k8s handoff flow. how are we reconciling pods with in-memory KV caches during drain?
ben.turner: I saw the same. quick notes: our current drain path does k8s cordon -> kubectl drain --force -> then scontrol requeue on slurm. For mixed-job workloads (k8s pod wrapping a slurm task) there is a race where the pod gets SIGTERM before the slurm job checkpoint completes.
carla.nguyen: idea: add a handoff-ack annotation and an ordered eviction handshake. sequence: 1) nodebot soft-cordon + mark 'handoff:starting' 2) owner controller attempts graceful checkpoint/save 3) owner writes annotation 'handoff:done' 4) nodebot proceeds to hard drain. this prevents losing KV caches.
alice.kim: exactly. also want cost-aware preference: if spare-pool capacity in same region exists, prefer remap instead of hard-evict to reduce recompute costs.
ben.turner: prototype event schema I used for testing:
```
{
  "event_id": "ecc-2331234567",
  "node": "eu-west1-gpu-12",
  "signals": ["ECC", "XID"],
  "severity": "burst",
  "state": "soft-cordon",
  "preferred_action": "handoff-or-remap",
  "timestamp": 2331234567
}
```
carla.nguyen: small k8s snippet for handoff ack (controller side):
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  annotations:
    redwood.io/handoff-status: "pending" # controller sets to 'done' when ckpt saved
```
matt.sre: for slurm side, we should scontrol hold then scontrol requeue after ack. example:
```
scontrol hold <jobid>
# wait for pod annotation redwood.io/handoff-status == done
scontrol release <jobid>
```
alice.kim: ops question: how long do we wait for handoff before fallback? propose 45s for small caches (<2GB), 3m for heavy jobs. can we make this SLO-driven per job label?
devops-oncall: +1. make it configurable via node annotation/cluster policy. also add a debounce that requires 2 consecutive ECC bursts within 30s to avoid noisy flaps.
ben.turner: will add reconciliation loop that is idempotent and tolerant to partial failures. if controller never ack, nodebot escalates to 'preserve-kv-epoch' snapshot flow and drains after snapshot written to local SSD.
carla.nguyen: I'll mock the annotation-based handshake in the staging cluster today. assigning: carla -> implement controller ack, ben -> nodebot changes for handoff state machine, matt -> slurm hold/release doc update, alice -> test scenarios + cost-remap policy.
alice.kim: thanks. let's keep this thread for infra runbook notes. please post brief test results here when done :thumbsup:
nodebot: note logged: action_plan=handoff-ack-handshake, owners=[carla.nguyen,ben.turner,matt.sre], ticket=INFRA-8442"
